decision: Use a deterministic fixed-point for generated imports
why: Attached import macros require expansion and graph discovery to converge without dropping imports
evidence: docs/adr/0003-compile-time-metaprogramming.md
result: documented

decision: Represent token literals as flat token pieces with temporary interpolation boundaries
why: Ordinary token content must stay unparsed while interpolation expressions need AST nodes
evidence: crates/nymph-ast/src/expr.rs; crates/nymph-syntax/tests/parser.rs
result: syntax tests green

decision: Expand declarations before semantic and graph consumers
why: Generated declarations and imports must enter the normal compiler pipeline
evidence: cargo test -p nymph-compiler --test project; cargo check --workspace --all-targets
result: 55 project tests green; workspace check green

decision: Reset deterministic budgets per root and eagerly validate const lets
why: The language requires every const let to evaluate even when unused, without unrelated roots consuming its budget
evidence: project tests for unused division by zero, separators, stacking; Node runtime const test
result: targeted tests green

decision: Use a 64-frame deterministic const call limit
why: A 256-frame recursive const call overflowed the compiler test thread before a diagnostic could be emitted
evidence: const_call_depth_limit_reports_an_expansion_trace
result: compiler reports META001 with trace instead of aborting

decision: Need a concrete std/meta representation and hygiene storage boundary
why: The settled behavior names construct types but does not define their fields/variants, while current Ident, Span, and NodeId cannot carry hygiene or expansion provenance
evidence: nymph-ast/src/lib.rs; stdlib/src/meta.nym; crates/nymph-compiler/src/metaprogramming.rs
result: request decision: public mirrored values vs opaque handles, and enriched AST values vs compiler side tables

decision: Carry syntax context and expansion origin in Span, and origin in NodeId
why: Tokens, identifiers, spans, and nodes must preserve hygiene/provenance through reparsing without authoritative side tables
evidence: metaprogramming unit tests; syntax tests; project tests; workspace check
result: contexts and deterministic origin IDs survive expansion and reparsing

decision: Resolve expansion traces from syntax-carried OriginId
why: Parser and semantic failures in generated output must report both invocation and definition spans
evidence: generated parse and type diagnostic project tests
result: both diagnostics include provenance notes

decision: Adapt declarations to public immutable records and a flat Declaration enum
why: Macros need ordinary pattern matching and field access without exposing the Rust AST as an ABI
evidence: broad and narrow attached-macro project tests; stdlib source check
result: declarations can be matched, inspected, rebuilt, and converted to tokens

decision: Accept Result success and structured diagnostic failures
why: Attached macros need recoverable user-facing errors anchored to typed syntax spans
evidence: result success and diagnostic span project tests
result: Result tokens expand; returned diagnostics keep the supplied span

decision: Expose optional and declaration-specific fields for all top-level declaration categories
why: Narrow attached targets must cover aliases and externals as well as core declarations
evidence: 68 project tests; stdlib source check; compiler clippy
result: alias/external target typing and immutable field adapters are green

decision: Expand each reachable const-import closure to a deterministic generated-import fixed point
why: Imported macros need definition-scope helpers and generated imports must join graph discovery without invalidating unrelated modules
evidence: 70 project tests; 8 incremental baseline tests; compiler clippy
result: private helpers resolve in their owner; generated import chains load; unrelated modules stay backdated

decision: Key semantic and stable identities by syntax context instead of changing identifier text
why: Definition-site and fresh names must coexist with caller names while exposed names bind at the call site
evidence: 72 project tests including Node execution; 102 sema tests; 8 incremental tests
result: definition-context helpers do not capture caller names; fresh names remain textually unchanged

decision: Preserve every diagnostic returned by a macro or generated parser
why: A diagnostic-list Result must not silently discard all but its first item
evidence: attached_macro_reports_every_returned_diagnostic
result: both returned diagnostics reach the project result in order

decision: Expand source tokens before contextual parsing while skipping token-literal bodies
why: One token prepass supports expression, type, pattern, statement, parameter, field, variant, and match-arm positions without placeholder AST variants
evidence: nested-destination Node test; generated-fragment test; 75 project tests; syntax tests
result: all nested destinations expand through the normal parser and runtime pipeline

decision: Add validated meta parse entry points and Function record serialization
why: Language-facing records must parse and rebuild syntax without exposing the Rust AST
evidence: typed_meta_functions_are_constructible_and_convert_back_to_tokens
result: constructed Function with parsed replacement body emits and runs

decision: Expose constructible flat Token values and full syntax context in Span
why: Public meta values must preserve syntax-carried hygiene and provenance through ordinary construction and conversion
evidence: public_meta_tokens_and_flat_token_variants_are_constructible; public_meta_span_constructor_preserves_context_and_origin
result: flat tokens emit runnable declarations; Span round-trips fresh context and origin

decision: Serialize public declaration and leaf records without dropping nested member tokens
why: Constructed immutable records and Declaration variants must re-enter parsing while retaining attached target contents
evidence: public_struct_and_declaration_records_rebuild_nested_members; 78 project tests
result: constructed Struct wrapped in Declaration preserves and runs its namespace member

decision: Interpret finite ranges, maps/indexing, closures, user ADTs, for loops, and state loops
why: Const functions are pure Nymph computations rather than token-template-only helpers
evidence: const_evaluation_supports_finite_collections_ranges_and_state_loops; 79 project tests; compiler clippy
result: mixed pure computation produces and runs the expected generated value under deterministic budgets

decision: Represent import roots and external declaration kinds explicitly in the public schema
why: Typed conversion must faithfully preserve graph-affecting import roots and distinguish external signatures
evidence: typed_import_records_rebuild_before_graph_discovery; external_declarations_expose_typed_function_and_let_variants
result: project-root import reconstruction joins graph discovery; external variants pattern-match before execution

decision: Resolve aliased std/meta type names before deciding runtime capability
why: Compile-time-only values must not leak merely because std/meta was imported under another namespace or with-name
evidence: aliased_meta_values_remain_compile_time_only; runtime_declarations_cannot_expose_aliased_meta_values
result: const meta declarations are erased and non-const meta signatures receive a diagnostic under aliases

decision: Preserve lexically valid contextual source insertions when no expansion environment is available
why: The standalone formatter cannot evaluate project-dependent const code and must not corrupt or reject valid pre-expansion source
evidence: cargo test -p nymph-format; preserves_unexpanded_insertions_at_contextual_grammar_destinations
result: whole-document and range formatting leave unresolved contextual insertions byte-stable

decision: Scope const and all three metaprogramming sigils before anonymous-dollar fallback
why: TextMate must remain useful when semantic AST roles are unavailable during an incomplete or unexpanded edit
evidence: pnpm --filter nymph test:unit
result: 23 extension unit tests pass; token capture, expansion, and attachment sigils have distinct scopes

decision: Exercise const expansion through the WASM compiler facade
why: The playground must use the same expansion pipeline rather than a syntax-only path
evidence: cargo test -p nymph-wasm
result: generated function appears in browser-target JavaScript with no diagnostics

decision: Assign compile-time-only std/meta after existing importable and ambient module slots
why: Adding meta must not renumber pre-existing emitted runtime bindings
evidence: cargo test -p nymph-compiler --features test-support --test stable_module_assembly stable_
result: all 16 stable assembly checks preserve their existing names and run

decision: Treat the raw source parse as the canonical tracked parse and track expanded imports separately
why: Expansion needs a second representation without reporting one source revision as two parse invalidations
evidence: session lifecycle and both LSP cache-count regression tests
result: changed roots and newly reachable modules reparse exactly once while unchanged analyses remain shared

decision: Use one compiler adapter for typed syntax, user Into implementations, and iterable flattening
why: Expansion and interpolation should accept the language protocol rather than concrete evaluator containers
evidence: project tests for typed destinations, custom Into, custom Iterable/Iterator, Result and separators
result: typed and user-defined values flatten deterministically while preserving token identity

decision: Represent intermediate attached output as one declaration or an ordered declaration collection
why: Multi-output inner macros must remain composable without weakening narrow target checks
evidence: multi-output stacked attachment and narrow mismatch tests
result: collection targets receive all declarations; narrow targets get labeled actionable diagnostics

decision: Attach help, const-call labels, and provenance labels before diagnostics reach CLI/LSP/WASM
why: Plain evaluator strings do not explain how to correct macro failures or where generated syntax originated
evidence: pretty render, generated parse/type, limit, conversion, and attachment tests
result: all META001 paths use standard structured diagnostics and generated errors retain expansion labels

decision: Retain the handwritten target once and evaluate every attachment independently against that same typed original
why: Attachments generate peer declarations; replacement and removal belong to direct expansion
evidence: independent attachment identity, order, zero/many, isolation, failure, mismatch, and collision tests
result: no collection handoff or sibling transformation pipeline remains
